name: Constructor (Artificer Archetype)
body:
A constructor sees constructs as the ultimate kind of undying creature. As such they find ways to modify and improve themselves by replacing parts with construct parts.

Constructed Arm (Ex)

At 1st level, a constructor replaces one of their arms with a construct’s arm. This arm is fully articulated and does not prevent any normal functions of using the arm, but grants the constructor a 1d6 slam attack. This slam attack can be used for multiple attacks as any weapon and you are proficient in its use. The constructed arm can be enchanted like any weapon and can be repaired if damaged. This arm cannot be disarmed. This ability replaces scribe scroll and trapfinding.

Embedded Paneling (Ex)

At 3rd level, a constructor has embedded protective plates that grant them a +2 bonus to their existing natural armor. This increases by a further +2 at 9th and 15th levels. This ability replaces all of the bonus metamagic feats.

Constructed Form (Ex)

At 7th level, a constructor has replaced so much of their base form that they can be targeted by spells that affect constructs or objects, including those that heal damage by repairing. This ability replaces metamagic spell trigger.

Ever-Living (Ex)

At 11th level, a constructor is more construct than they are person. They are no longer healed by spells that heal living creatures, but they are immune to poison and disease. They also no longer age. At 16th level, they are also immune to death effects. This ability replaces metamagic spell completion.
